Agents Come With Kolu (agent-distro)

Features·seedling·accepted·OCT 06, 2026

Kolu puts agent-distro's coding agents, with kolu's own plugin, on the PATH of every new terminal on every host — one Settings choice (the profile), a per-tile chip, and hosts that download their own agents. ADK1 shipped; ADK2–ADK4 follow.

Contents

  • The shape
  • ADK1 — Choose your agents in Settings (implemented)
  • ADK2–ADK4 — next

Run kolu, open a terminal on any host, type claude — it runs. So do codex, omp, opencode and pi, each with kolu’s plugin loaded. They come from agent-distro, which kolu pins and names in Settings; the one choice a user makes is the profile. User docs: kolu.dev/agents.

The plan of record spans two repositories (agent-distro’s U0–U4, kolu’s ADK1–ADK4) and lives with the planner; this note records kolu’s side. ADK1 is implemented; ADK2–ADK4 are not started.

The shape

Two repositories, one promise. agent-distro owns the agents: which harnesses exist, what a profile adds, how a bundle is updated. kolu owns the one user decision and puts that profile’s harnesses on the PATH of every new terminal, on every host. Kolu consumes agent-distro across a process boundary — its Nix library at build time, its --list --json and its updater at run time — and never imports its code.The process boundary is what works on a remote host, where padi is the only kolu process, and it keeps the two repos independently releasable. Kolu’s plugin reaches every harness at launch through AGENT_DISTRO_PLUGINS (agent-distro’s U2), so it is present in any profile and any bundle version without agent-distro pinning kolu.

layer owns
preference agentDistro (kolu-server conf, 1.37.0) on/off + profile, global
kolu-server cell agentDistroListing the profiles, read once from the baked picker
padi cell agentDistro (memory-only, pushed) the setting, per host, re-pushed on every connect
padi cell agentDistroStatus ready · downloading · error · off · unavailable
padi spawn resolve the bundle, pin it on the record, put its bin/ on PATH
nix/agent-distro.nix the floor bundle, per-profile updater configs, the plugin dir

ADK1 — Choose your agents in Settings (implemented)

Shipped in #2265.

  • One setting, global. A kolu preference, pushed into each bound padi by the same mechanism as the new-terminal theme policy (padiCellPusher.ts). padi refuses a profile its build does not know; the UI shows an unknown stored profile as an error and never resets it.
  • New terminals only, each one says which. At spawn padi resolves the host’s <state>/current if the updater put one there, else the floor kolu ships (local machine only). The exact store path is stamped on the terminal record (agentProfile / agentBundle) and its bin/ joins the toolchain after kolu’s own tools, riding the KOLU_TERMINAL_TOOLS_PATH stamp. The tile chip shows the profile and the bundle’s short hash.
  • Off means off. Nothing on PATH, no plugin variable, no chip.
  • Hosts download their own agents. padi-agent carries no floor. On first use padi runs agent-distro’s lib.mkUpdater command (its config made concrete for the host’s state home), which fetches from the binary cache into the host’s store; the host tab shows its --progress byte counts and a toast announces “Agents ready”. No retry loop.
  • Nix. agent-distro is an npins pin, no flake input. The floor is built with kolu’s nixpkgs via agent-distro’s own mkLaunchers / mkPicker, exposed as agent-distro-bundle (so the cache job pushes it), and baked only on the default wrapper. x86_64-darwin left kolu’s systems.

Known limits are decided, not open: garbage collection can remove an old bundle under a running agent; two updaters on one machine are harmless; a fetched (remote) bundle has no agent-distro picker of its own; a host fetches github:juspay/agent-distro at its latest main, while padi checks a profile name against the listing pinned in kolu’s build, so a profile added upstream is refused until kolu’s pin moves.

ADK2–ADK4 — next

  • ADK2 · First run asks. A step in the welcome flow bound to the same preference, shown only while it has never been written.
  • ADK3 · Agents stay current. padi runs the updater four times a day on every host and flips current; Settings shows versions and history; a landed update toasts.
  • ADK4 · The terminal tells you the next move (optional). One tip in the tile’s title bar from a terminal’s live facts.
